fields.sections.1.h: Free provision of complete lecture videos
fields.sections.0.ko: Carnegie Mellon University opens lectures covering diverse topics including artificial intelligence, robotics, systems, and bioinformatics from multiple departments. Faculty from seven leading departments directly teach, structured around actual courses at the university. This represents an effort to open the elite educational assets of a prestigious university to a broad general audience.
fields.sections.1.ko: Anyone can freely watch complete lecture videos conducted by Carnegie Mellon faculty. By capturing the actual classroom setting, it aims to similarly convey the quality of education experienced by actual students. This is an attempt to increase accessibility to higher education.
fields.sections.2.ko: Along with lecture videos, assignments and practice problems used in actual Carnegie Mellon courses are provided. Learners receive immediate feedback after solving, and can earn badges upon completing assignments, boosting learning motivation. It is designed to provide formal learning experience while remaining a free platform.
fields.sections.3.ko: A future platform update plans to add an artificial intelligence-based personalized tutoring system. When learners encounter difficulties solving problems, AI intervenes to provide concept explanations and solution methods. This is an effort to supplement with advanced technology the endemic problem of large-scale online education: insufficient feedback per student.
fields.sections.4.ko: Beyond free lectures, official credentials can be obtained through graded assignment submission and Carnegie Mellon's online program. A paid advanced pathway is being prepared for learners who want more systematic learning and demonstrable achievement. A layered model of free accessibility and paid advanced courses is being utilized.
fields.sections.5.ko: Carnegie Mellon's School of Computing also operates executive education programs for organization-level instruction. Beyond individual learners, the school supports organizations seeking to enhance expertise by running curriculum at the team level. The university is expanding its educational assets in B2B fashion as well.
fields.sections.6.ko: Carnegie Mellon offers a full-time degree program for admission as an undergraduate to the Kenneth C. Griffin School of Computing, in parallel with the online platform. Free open lectures ultimately become an opportunity for prospective students considering admission to the university to experience the institution's educational level.
fields.sections.7.ko: The CS Learn platform is developed and led by Carnegie Mellon undergraduates, operated with support from Scottie Labs, a student organization. By having the university's technology community participate with a sense of ownership, sustainable development and a student-centered improvement culture are being formed.
fields.caveat: The source is an official announcement introducing platform features and plans, so separate monitoring is needed regarding actual implementation timing and completeness of planned features such as AI tutoring, and how free lectures actually connect with U.S. foreign university admissions.
